articles.title: Gaza residents watch Israel election, hoping to unseat Netanyahu as airstrikes continue
articles.description: Residents of Gaza’s southern city of Khan Younis are closely watching Israel’s election. They hope that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu loses but doubt a change in leadership will significantly improve their lives. Some favor challenger Gadi Eisenkot. He is a supporter U.S. President Donald Trump’s Gaza road map plan. Others see little difference between the candidates’ policies. Israeli strikes in Khan Younis on Wednesday killed one Palestinian and wounded at least six others to underscore the residents' fears. Gaza health officials say Israeli forces have killed more than 1,550 Palestinians since the truce began in October 2025. Immediate concerns about food, shelter and security are top priorities for many residents.

articles.title: Gaza Residents Watch Israel Election, Hoping to Unseat Netanyahu as Airstrikes Continue
articles.description: DEIR AL-BALAH, Gaza Strip (AP) — In the southern Gaza Strip, where Israeli airstrikes are still a regular occurrence despite a ceasefire, residents of the city of Khan Younis were following the results of Israel’s election closely, hoping that anyone but Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will form the next government.

articles.title: Israel Election: Netanyahu claims ‘decisive majority’ as exit polls show deadlock
articles.description: Israel's first national election since the October 2023 Hamas attacks ends in a close race between Netanyahu and Eisenkot, with no clear majority and high voter turnout shaping coalition talks.

articles.title: Projections show no clear winner in Israel's election
articles.description: Israelis turned out in record numbers for their first election since the Oct. 7 attacks and the war in Gaza. Projections show opposition parties won more seats than the coalition led by Prime Minister Netanyahu, potentially setting the stage for a change in government. But Netanyahu’s opponents do not have enough seats to form a majority, leading to weeks of negotiations. Nick Schifrin reports.
